requirement: Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.
problem_statement: Deliver a stateless HTTP service that maps long URLs to short codes, redirects with low latency, persists links durably, and reports per-link click analytics, with explicit numeric scale targets and abuse protection.

ambiguities.question: What load must it sustain (requests/sec, links, data size) and what latency target applies?
ambiguities.assumption: Target ~1,000 redirects/s and 50 creates/s per node, p95 redirect < 50 ms; scale out by adding stateless nodes.

ambiguities.question: Which metrics (totals, time series, referrers, geo, unique visitors) and what retention?
ambiguities.assumption: Total clicks, clicks per day, top referrer hosts and device class; raw events kept, no IP/geo stored.

ambiguities.question: REST, GraphQL or gRPC? Who authenticates and how are errors reported?
ambiguities.assumption: JSON REST over HTTP, OpenAPI documented, optional API key on management endpoints.

ambiguities.question: Which datastore, durability and retention requirements apply?
ambiguities.assumption: SQLite behind a repository interface for the prototype; the schema ports to PostgreSQL.

assumptions: scalable: Target ~1,000 redirects/s and 50 creates/s per node, p95 redirect < 50 ms; scale out by adding stateless nodes.
analytics: Total clicks, clicks per day, top referrer hosts and device class; raw events kept, no IP/geo stored.
apis: JSON REST over HTTP, OpenAPI documented, optional API key on management endpoints.
persistence: SQLite behind a repository interface for the prototype; the schema ports to PostgreSQL.

tasks.title: Clarify requirement, scale targets and analytics scope

ai_assist.prompt: Requirement: "Build a scalable URL shortener service with APIs, persistence, and analytics.". Identify ambiguities in 'scalable', 'persistence' and 'analytics'. Propose measurable targets and a minimal analytics set.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Chooses targets and records them as assumptions.

ai_assist.prompt: Draft an OpenAPI 3 contract for a URL shortener: create (custom alias, expiry), fetch, delete, analytics, redirect (302). Define 404/409/410/422/429 semantics.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Chooses 302 over 301 (analytics must see every click) and the status code for each failure.

tasks.title: Design persistence schema

ai_assist.prompt: Design a relational schema for short links and click events supporting redirect lookup by code and per-day aggregation. Explain indexes.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Validates keys, cascade rules and that the hot path is one indexed lookup.

validation: Redirect lookup is a primary-key read
Deleting a link removes its clicks

ai_assist.prompt: Implement collision-safe short code generation and strict URL validation (scheme allow-list, no credentials, no private hosts, length limits).
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Reviews randomness source (secrets, not random), collision retry and SSRF/open-redirect risks.

tasks.title: Implement persistence layer

ai_assist.prompt: Implement a repository over the schema with create/get/delete/record_click/analytics queries; parameterised SQL only.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Checks parameterisation, transaction scope and locking behaviour.

validation: Concurrent click recording does not lose counts

tasks.title: Implement service layer: create, resolve, expire, cache

ai_assist.prompt: Implement the service orchestrating validation, persistence, expiry checks and a read-through cache invalidated on delete.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Reviews cache invalidation, expiry correctness and clock handling.

validation: Deleted link never served from cache

ai_assist.prompt: Implement the OpenAPI contract with FastAPI. Record clicks in a background task so redirects stay fast.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Confirms behaviour matches the contract and analytics cannot block redirects.

ai_assist.prompt: Capture referrer host and device class per click (no raw IP), expose totals, per-day series, top referrers and devices for a window.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Decides privacy boundary (what is NOT stored) and verifies aggregation maths.

ai_assist.prompt: Review the shortener for abuse: enumeration, alias squatting, SSRF via targets, unbounded input, rate-limit bypass. Provide findings.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Triages each finding and decides the mitigation or accepted risk.

ai_assist.prompt: Create a small load script for the redirect path and summarise bottlenecks and the path to PostgreSQL/Redis for horizontal scale.
ai_assist.ai_role: Writes the benchmark and drafts scaling notes.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Interprets numbers honestly (prototype vs production hardware).

ai_assist.prompt: Write pytest tests for validation, generator, repository, cache, service, API and analytics including expiry, alias conflicts and concurrent clicks.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Verifies tests can fail, removes weak assertions, owns the coverage threshold.

ai_assist.prompt: Draft README, architecture and runbook from the code. Mark any statement you cannot verify.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Runs every documented command and fixes mistakes.

ai_assist.prompt: Review the whole change as a skeptical maintainer: correctness, security, maintainability, test gaps.
ai_assist.engineer_owns: Owns merge decision and limitations list.

risks.mitigation: UNIQUE constraint plus bounded retry; 62^7 (~3.5e12) code space makes collisions rare.

risks.risk: Expired or deleted links still redirecting because of caching.
risks.mitigation: Expiry is re-checked on every cache hit; delete invalidates the cache; TTL bounds staleness on other nodes.

risks.risk: Single SQLite writer limits write throughput and horizontal scale.
risks.mitigation: Repository interface isolates SQL; documented migration to PostgreSQL + Redis cache.

risks.risk: Click recording on the redirect path could add latency or lose events on crash.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in a background task; accepted trade-off of possible loss on crash (analytics, not billing).

risks.risk: Open redirect / SSRF abuse through attacker-chosen targets.
risks.mitigation: Scheme allow-list, no credentials, no private/loopback hosts, rate limiting, optional API key.
Acceptance criteria and assumptions are written down and reviewed before coding.
Smallest design satisfying the criteria; extension points documented, not built.

risks.risk: Edge cases and error paths are untested.
risks.mitigation: Tests for boundaries and failures are written for every task; coverage gate in CI.

risks.risk: AI output looks plausible but is incorrect or uses non-existent APIs.
risks.mitigation: Every generated unit is run, type-checked and covered by tests before acceptance.

risks.risk: AI-written tests may be tautological and miss gaps (coverage illusion).
risks.mitigation: Engineer breaks the code deliberately to confirm tests fail; coverage is a floor, not proof.

risks.risk: Inefficient or insecure patterns (N+1 queries, string-built SQL, weak randomness).
risks.mitigation: Checklist review for SQL, randomness, input validation and complexity; separate AI review pass.

risks.risk: Sensitive data or proprietary code exposed to AI tools.
risks.mitigation: Prompts contain requirements and snippets only; no secrets or customer data.

trade_offs.rationale: Zero-setup, runnable prototype; the interface keeps migration cheap. Limited write concurrency.
No coordination between nodes and codes are non-enumerable; needs collision retry.
301 is cached by browsers, which would hide clicks and make delete/expiry ineffective.
Keeps redirect latency low; may drop events on crash. A queue is the production upgrade.
No extra infrastructure; per-node caches can be stale up to the TTL.
Simple and testable; limits are per node.
Reproducible and reviewable; less flexible. LLM output would still need engineer review.

trade_offs.chosen: Contract and tests before wide implementation
trade_offs.rationale: Slower start, fewer rework cycles and clearer acceptance criteria.

limitations: Plans are templates tailored by keyword detection, not deep semantic understanding.
AI prompts are generated for an engineer to run in Copilot/ChatGPT; the tool calls no model itself.
